findings.claim: “For OCR Component 01 Section A, this context is essential… Part (b) asks a broader question about the whole text.”
findings.truth: “Component 01” is on the house banned list and rejects the whole unit at validation. The structure itself is right — one compulsory two-part question, part (a) a comparison of a printed extract with an unseen modern prose extract, part (b) a related question on the same studied text — so only the code and the loose wording of part (b) needed replacing.
findings.evidence: specs/ocr/english-literature-J352.md lines 1710-1760 (forms of assessment); CHECK_PROMPT.md banned-string list.

findings.claim: All 48 practice questions (6 in each of the 8 lessons) carry the split “AO1 (up to 8) / AO2 (up to 8) / AO3 (up to 4)”, followed by a six-band ladder “Top band (19-20) / Upper band (15-18) / Upper-mid band (11-14) / Mid band (7-10) / Lower-mid band (3-6) / Lower band (1-2)”.
findings.truth: The spec publishes no marking grid and no per-question AO split; it gives only component-level weightings (Component 01: AO1 20%, AO2 17.5%, AO3 10%, AO4 2.5% of the qualification) and states AO4 is assessed in Section B only. An 8/8/4 split is invented. The ladder is also malformed: six bands, unequal widths, and two band names (“Upper band”, “Lower band”) that are not in the house set. Every string is now the house one-liner plus five equal bands for 20 marks (17-20 / 13-16 / 9-12 / 5-8 / 1-4), matching the sibling OCR units.
findings.evidence: specs/ocr/english-literature-J352.md lines 1710-1760 and 1836-1960 (AO weightings table; AO4 in Section B of each component). No marking grid in the spec.

findings.claim: “The animals are confused but lack the confidence to argue: ‘If Comrade Napoleon says it, it must be right.’”, with flashcard 11 asking “Which phrase does the confused animals chant under pressure?”
findings.truth: The line is Boxer's, spoken once in chapter 7 after Squealer states that Snowball was Jones's agent from the beginning. It is not a chant and the animals do not say it. The lesson also places it in a chapters 4-6 lesson without naming the chapter.
findings.evidence: animal-farm.txt line 1657 (ch. 7): “‘Ah, that is different!’ said Boxer. ‘If Comrade Napoleon says it, it must be right.’”

findings.claim: Knowledge check 2 asks what replaces ‘Beasts of England’ and keys the answer “A new anthem praising Napoleon”. Lesson 4 prose calls the replacement a “personality cult anthem” (twice) and says “the revolution’s ideals have been replaced by worship of the leader”; flashcard 3 repeats it; lesson 7 says “The replacement anthem, praising Napoleon…” and “Napoleon replaces it with a personality cult anthem”.
findings.truth: Minimus's chapter 7 replacement praises the FARM: “Animal Farm, Animal Farm, / Never through me shalt thou come to harm!” The cult-of-personality piece is the separate chapter 8 poem “Comrade Napoleon”, inscribed on the barn wall under a portrait. The knowledge check therefore marks a wrong answer as correct. The same error was found in the AQA and Edexcel Animal Farm units.
findings.evidence: animal-farm.txt lines 1805-1812 (ch. 7, Minimus's song) and 1878-1908 (ch. 8, the poem ‘Comrade Napoleon’ and its inscription).

findings.claim: “Benjamin, who can read, raises the alarm: ‘They are taking you to your death!’”
findings.truth: Misattributed. Benjamin reads the van and says “They are taking Boxer to the knacker’s!” It is Clover, chasing the van, who cries “Boxer! Get out! Get out quickly! They’re taking you to your death!”

findings.claim: “Squealer announces that Boxer died peacefully in hospital, with Napoleon at his side.”
findings.truth: Squealer claims HE was at the bedside: “I was at his bedside at the very last.” Napoleon is not present and only speaks about Boxer at the meeting on the following Sunday.

findings.claim: Quotation bank: “‘Your lives are miserable, laborious, and short’ (Old Major’s rhetoric).”
findings.truth: Old Major says “Our lives are miserable, laborious, and short” — he includes himself, which is the point of the rhetoric. Lesson 2 quotes it correctly, so the memorisation list teaches the wrong version for a closed-text exam.

findings.claim: “if your paper pairs an extract from Animal Farm with an unseen prose extract…”; “Check your exam board’s specimen paper for the exact question wording and timing guidance”; “Check your exam board’s specimen paper for exact timings and mark weightings.”
findings.truth: Board-agnostic hedging on a board-specific unit. The format is fixed and known: a closed-text two-hour paper of two 40-mark sections, so about an hour on the modern prose question; part (a) always prints an extract beside an unseen modern prose extract; the two parts are 20 marks each; and there is no spelling and punctuation credit in this section because AO4 sits in the 19th-century prose section.
findings.evidence: specs/ocr/english-literature-J352.md lines 1710-1760 (two-hour closed-text paper, 40 + 40) and the AO4 statement in section 3h.

findings.claim: Flashcard 12: “What is an embedded quotation, the OCR-preferred quotation style?”
findings.truth: The spec states no preferred quotation style. Embedding is good advice, but naming it a board preference invents a rule.
findings.evidence: specs/ocr/english-literature-J352.md — no such statement anywhere in the assessment sections.

findings.claim: Squealer: “Milk and apples contain substances absolutely necessary to the well-being of a pig.” (prose and flashcard 10)
findings.truth: The real line is “Milk and apples (this has been proved by Science, comrades) contain substances absolutely necessary to the well-being of a pig.” The parenthesis is dropped without an ellipsis, but every word quoted is Orwell's and no examiner would penalise it. Not worth re-narrating a block.

findings.claim: “Napoleon sells him to the knacker for whisky money” (key fact and flashcard 3).
findings.truth: Orwell keeps this as rumour, not statement: “the word went round that from somewhere or other the pigs had acquired the money to buy themselves another case of whisky.” It is the standard and intended inference, so it is left alone — the same call was made on the AQA unit.

findings.claim: “Napoleon announces that Boxer will be sent to a hospital.”
findings.truth: Squealer makes the announcement; the arrangement is attributed to Napoleon. The distinction matters slightly because every message reaches the animals through Squealer, but it is not mark-affecting.

findings.claim: “Napoleon proclaims victory and celebrates with the other pigs by getting drunk.”
findings.truth: Two separate events are compressed. The victory brought two days of celebrations; the whisky was found in the farmhouse cellar “a few days later than this”. The order of events is otherwise right and the point about the altered alcohol commandment stands.

findings.claim: Lesson 2 is titled “Chapters 1-3: The Rebellion” but its fourth section is “The Battle of the Cowshed (Chapter 4)”, which lesson 3 (“Chapters 4-6”) also claims.
findings.truth: Chapter 4 is covered twice and the lesson 2 title under-states its range. The prose names the chapter honestly each time, so nothing is factually wrong; titles are not editable through _edits.json.
findings.evidence: raw/L02.txt heading n11; raw/L03.txt heading n1.

findings.claim: Lesson 2 description is 106 characters: “Old Major’s speech, the Seven Commandments, the Rebellion, the Battle of the Cowshed and early corruption.”
findings.truth: The house validator caps a lesson description under 100 characters. The other seven descriptions in this unit are 87-97 characters. Not a fact error, so nothing is edited, but it will trip the validator if that gate is enforced.

summary: Eight lessons checked against the Gutenberg text and the spec. The exam framing was almost sound (closed text, two-part 20+20 modern prose question, no SPaG claim, no Paper/Component mislabelling beyond one banned string), but every one of the 48 practice questions carried an invented AO1 8 / AO2 8 / AO3 4 split over a malformed six-band ladder. The content errors are a small cluster: the chapter 7 replacement anthem is repeatedly said to praise Napoleon when it praises the farm (one knowledge check keyed wrong), Clover's cry to Boxer is given to Benjamin, Squealer's bedside claim is given to Napoleon, Boxer's “If Comrade Napoleon says it” is given to the animals as a chant, and the lesson 8 quotation bank misquotes Old Major's opening tricolon.
